title: Explicit scheduling metrics
text: The browser's FIFO/SJF/RR metrics match the freshly compiled C scheduler on the bounded explicit 5,2,3 job list, quantum 2. All arrivals are zero. This does not establish exact CLI/output/random parity with scheduler.py.

title: Scheduler input and parity boundaries
text: The C source does not implement the reference's -h option, and rand() differs from Python's seeded generator. Its parsing accepts malformed/zero lists without robust validation; RR with a nonpositive quantum may not progress. The new browser validates positive inputs and makes no exact-port-compliance claim.

title: Early allocator failure is preserved
text: Fresh hashproj.c builds completed empty, ABBA and one-block A fixtures in single/fork modes. A 2,050-byte banana-bandana fixture caused signal 11 in single mode, while fork mode returned 1996215911. This is a bounded observed failure, not a claim that every multi-block input crashes. Its free/coalescing size conventions warrant review; no native fix is silently substituted.

title: Later bounded signatures agree
text: Fresh sharedhash and experimental esharedhash builds completed the same four fixtures in single, fork and thread modes with matching signatures. Small fixture agreement is useful evidence but does not prove memory safety, race freedom or performance at scale.

title: Fork copies private memory
text: The later init_umem uses malloc with a regular free-list pointer, and allocator locking is enabled only for threads. Its -m children therefore have private copy-on-write heaps, not a concurrently shared allocator protected by an interprocess semaphore. Old comments describing shared mmap/semaphores no longer describe this implementation. A child's inherited stack snapshot is not overwritten merely because its parent later changes its own stack.

title: Fork is not automatically parallel work
text: hashproj's parent reads each result pipe immediately before creating the next child, serializing the main per-block computation path. The later run_multi creates children first and collects later. The website distinguishes orchestration from measured CPU parallelism.

title: The signature is intentionally weak
text: Within a block, the algorithm depends on frequencies rather than byte order. ABBA and BABA yield the same tree signature. Block signatures are added, so reordering whole blocks also preserves the final sum. Do not use it as cryptographic integrity evidence.

title: Compile-time experiment affects all modes
text: In esharedhash.c, halloc/hfree switch at compile time under EXPERIMENTAL_ALLOC. They do not consult use_std_alloc_for_huffman, although main assigns that variable. The compiled switch therefore affects Huffman allocations in every mode, not just -t. Block-buffer allocation still follows umalloc.

title: Two recorded timing pairs
text: part-2 result.png records 3.381/0.464 seconds, about 7.29×. part-2_results.png and markdown.md record 3.839/0.432 seconds, about 8.89× (reported as 8.88×). All show signature 2047368427. These are distinct archived runs; no new timing reproduction or general scalability proof is claimed.

title: Performance conclusions need measurements
text: The report's greater-than-90% lock-traffic claim and attribution of the entire gain to contention are not backed by lock counters or a controlled repeated benchmark in the archive. System/user times can add across threads. Matching one faux signature is not universal semantic equivalence. The report remains visible with these qualifications.

title: MLFQ share claims have assumptions
text: The archived Q11 uses top quantum 10 ms and B≤200 ms to argue a 5% share. That heuristic assumes the job actually receives a full top-queue slice per boost period. Arbitrary ready sets, queue order and I/O patterns can invalidate a universal guarantee. The simplified browser omits these complexities and does not certify all eleven answers.

title: Scaffold constraints are version-specific
text: The archive includes a full open-ended experimental prompt and a V002 assignment wrapper restricting changes to allocator-related functions. The report's external allocation wrappers must be assessed against the applicable instructor revision. No grading/compliance conclusion is inferred from these differing documents.
